title: Terminal
suits: developer tools, infrastructure, CLIs, APIs, SDKs, security and devops: products whose users live in a shell

params.--field: the field (phosphor green by default; any colour or gradient)
params.--brand: cursor and mark (used if it reads on the field)
params.--brand-2: a tint for the text (applied only while the text stays at 7:1), and the fallback accent
params.--term-fs / --term-mono: final wordmark size / typed text size
params.BOOT: the boot lines in the script: short, generic texture
params.__MARK__: stroke paths in a 24 x 24 box; it is what the prompt glyph becomes

details: before the press the field already shows a prompt and an idle cursor blinking at 1.06 s
the cursor holds solid while keys are typing and only blinks when idle, as real terminals do
keystrokes land with human rhythm: uneven gaps, an occasional hesitation
two thirds in, a finger slips onto the neighbouring key; a beat, a backspace, the right key
the slipped character leaves a phosphor ghost that fades for a fifth of a second
enter commits the line with a brief brightness flash
boot lines print faster than anyone can read, the log scrolling one line at a time, with a small [######] bar
the log flicks away line by line, top first
every typed letter flies from its mono slot into its slot in the wordmark, crossfading typefaces, staggered
the prompt glyph flies across and becomes the mark
the cursor ends after the wordmark in the accent and keeps blinking on the deck clock
faint scanlines and a vignette; the text glows only when the ink is light (a dark glow would read as a smudge)
long names type faster so the reveal still lands inside 2.4 s
